facts.statement: Denazinosuchus is classified as a goniopholidid mesoeucrocodylian.
facts.quote: Denazinosuchus is a genus of goniopholidid mesoeucrocodylian.

facts.statement: The species was first described in 1932 by Carl Wiman as Goniopholis kirtlandicus based on skull material.
facts.quote: It was first described in 1932 by Carl Wiman on the basis of a skull as a species of Goniopholis, G. kirtlandicus.

facts.statement: Spencer G. Lucas and Robert M. Sullivan redescribed the species in 2003, elevating it to the genus Denazinosuchus.
facts.quote: Spencer G. Lucas and Robert M. Sullivan redescribed the species in 2003 and gave it its own genus, Denazinosuchus.

facts.statement: Fossils of Denazinosuchus come from the Upper Cretaceous Fruitland and Kirtland Formations in the San Juan Basin, New Mexico, dating to the late Campanian to early Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been recovered from the Upper Cretaceous Fruitland Formation and Kirtland Formation (late Campanian-early Maastrichtian) of the San Juan Basin, New Mexico.

facts.statement: Currently, Denazinosuchus is known only from skull material, armor plates, and a thigh bone.
facts.quote: To date, Denazinosuchus is only known from skull material, armor, and a thigh bone.

facts.statement: Denazinosuchus lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Denazinosuchus belongs to the family Goniopholididae.
Denazinosuchus is classified within the class Reptilia.
A 2025 phylogenetic study by Platt and colleagues recovered Paarthurnax as the sister taxon to Denazinosuchus.
facts.quote: In their 2025 description of Paarthurnax, Platt and colleagues recovered this taxon as the sister to Denazinosuchus.

rejected.statement: Denazinosuchus is the most abundant and identifiable crocodylomorph in the San Juan Basin, characterized by distinctive subrectangular, flattened, and sparsely pitted bony armor.
rejected.quote: It is the most abundant and readily identifiable mesoeucrocodylian of the San Juan Basin, mostly due to its distinctive subrectangular, flattened, and sparsely pitted bony armor.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'distinctive subrectangular flattened and sparsely pitted bony armor'
